# SGLang/TileLang QSA score donor

SparkServe borrows the Qwen QSA paged-decode score kernel generated by
SGLang at immutable commit
`d91c3682b0b429e4c70df63cd57f819588ce29b0` using TileLang 0.1.11 at
`cd37ed5fc35ae7a60a1277c8eb49028174ac51e6`.

- SGLang source: `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/mqa.py`
- SGLang source SHA-256:
  `af36d5c8f4fbda5b0e82b7f31046a95c9a709fcc57b3600c6473c49e87b7629f`
- generated CUDA SHA-256:
  `52697eae776dba3b8212f8d6be75e8b1a6e574558dd9735293a2890f65d567d4`
- SGLang license: Apache-2.0
- TileLang CUDA templates: MIT; the upstream license is retained as `LICENSE`

`generated/device_kernel.cu` is the unmodified output for the live Qwen
specialization: eight padded BF16 query heads, head dimension 128, compressed
page size 16, 64 score rows per CTA, 128 threads, and 18,432 bytes of dynamic
shared memory. The `include/tl_templates/cuda` directory is the corresponding
header subtree from the pinned TileLang wheel. FlashInfer's already-pinned
CUTLASS headers satisfy the template dependency.

`csrc/cuda/qsa_score_tilelang.cu` removes the generated TVM-FFI host wrapper and
JIT dependency. It includes the generated device source unchanged, renames its
generic symbol at preprocessing time, and launches it through SparkServe's raw
C ABI on a Rust-owned stream. Rust owns the coherent query, compressed-cache,
page-table, context-length, and logits slabs. The kernel only writes score
positions below each context length; the following radix-top-k stage consumes
the same lengths, so no full logits fill is required.

The private fixture is generated by `scripts/capture-qsa-score-fixture.py` and
covers one-token, 64-key-boundary, and final-partial-group rows.
On GB10 it matches all 329 valid FP32 score values bit-for-bit and takes 4.11
microseconds mean for the three-row fixture. The joined fixture in
`scripts/capture-qsa-decode-chain-fixture.py` additionally feeds this output
through selection, K/V packing, and XQA under Rust's six stage leases.
